metadata.title: AI Ecosystem Governance, Economic & Architecture Model
metadata.description: Property graph of the AI ecosystem: value chain, control structure (viewpoint-relative VSM frames), liability, adversaries and named feedback loops, with Wardley evolution stage on value-chain components.
metadata.provenance_note: Cardinalities are order-of-magnitude estimates and are unsourced; weaker ones are flagged confidence: low. Sources are attached only to claims checked on 2026-11-15 (EU AI Act fine tiers, GPAI fining powers, safety-institute names). Other EU AI Act article references (e.g. Art. 12, 14, 43, 85) are unverified; check against the current consolidated text.

clusters.label: 0. Jurisdictional, Capital & Regulatory Sphere
clusters.description: Authorities, standards and certification bodies, safety institutes, insurers and capital markets.

clusters.label: 1. Upstream Silicon, Energy, Cloud, Data & Model Supply
clusters.description: Semiconductors, energy, compute campuses, hyperscalers, training data, frontier labs and models, open commons.

clusters.label: 2. Application & Agent Domain
clusters.description: AI applications, agent runtimes, guardrails, audit ledgers and observability.

clusters.label: 3. Enterprise Deployer & Principal Domain
clusters.description: Enterprise principal, AI governance function, identity, knowledge stores and human overseers.

clusters.label: 4. Execution Environment, Blast Radius & Adversaries
clusters.description: Tool gateways, target systems, affected individuals and hostile actors.

nodes.label: Statutory & Trade Authorities
nodes.sublabel: EU AI Office & national authorities, FTC/state AGs, BIS export controls, China CAC, UK & APAC regulators

properties.gpai_fine_powers: Commission fining powers over GPAI providers apply from 2 Aug 2026 (GPAI obligations since 2 Aug 2025)
properties.enforcement_powers: EU: fines up to 7% of global turnover for prohibited practices (Art. 99), up to 3% for GPAI providers (Art. 101); US: ex-post enforcement, litigation, export-control sanctions; China: registration and licensing regimes; stop orders.

nodes.label: Standards Setting Organisations
nodes.sublabel: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42, NIST, CEN-CENELEC, IEEE

properties.harmonization_role: Harmonised European standards (hENs) and ISO/IEC 42001 AIMS controls
properties.variety_function: Attenuates technical variety into standardised conformity benchmarks

nodes.label: AI Safety & Security Institutes
nodes.sublabel: US CAISI (formerly AISI), UK AI Security Institute, Japan AISI, frontier evaluators

properties.red_team_role: Pre-deployment red-teaming, bio/cyber capability evaluations, systemic-risk thresholds

nodes.label: Conformity & Certification Bodies
nodes.sublabel: EU notified bodies, ISO/IEC 42001 certifiers

properties.reassessment_authority: Recognition and supervision by statutory authorities; evidence from enterprise-operated systems is not independent of the assessed enterprise
properties.role: EU conformity assessment where a notified body is required (Art. 43; most Annex III systems use internal control instead) and voluntary ISO/IEC 42001 certification

nodes.label: AI Risk Underwriter & Insurer
nodes.sublabel: Algorithmic liability and cyber risk carriers

nodes.label: Capital Markets & Venture Underwriters

nodes.label: Legislatures & Executive Policy-Makers
nodes.sublabel: EU Parliament & Council, US Congress & executive, national parliaments, ministries

properties.role: Sets objectives, statutory mandates and funding; ultimate policy closure for each regime

nodes.label: Courts & Dispute Resolution
nodes.sublabel: National and EU courts, arbitration, class-action mechanisms

properties.role: Interprets statute and adjudicates liability and redress

nodes.label: Civil Society, Researchers & Media

properties.role: Surfaces harm and holds institutions to account; the public alarm channel when formal channels are slow

nodes.label: Energy Grids & Power Generation

loops.label: Capital-compute-valuation flywheel
loops.description: Capital funds lab compute commitments; compute yields capability and valuation uplift, which attracts more capital. Drives concentration.

loops.label: Open-release margin brake
loops.description: Labs that release open weights seed commodity inference, which compresses their own premium margins.

loops.label: Harm-complaint-enforcement loop
loops.description: Harm triggers complaints and enforcement, the enterprise tightens guardrails, constraining agent actions on target systems.

loops.label: Social-licence loop
loops.description: Harm drives churn and reputational cost; the enterprise tightens guardrails without waiting for the regulator.

loops.label: Harm-alarm-policy loop
loops.description: Systemic harm reaches the legislature through the algedonic channel, widening mandates and enforcement. Slow, but it bypasses regulatory capture.

frames.label: Enterprise AI operations (recursion level 0)
frames.description: One enterprise's AI-enabled operations. The knowledge store is a resource of S1 and is not given a role.
frames.system_boundary: Inside: agents, controls, audit, observability, AI governance and the enterprise principal. Outside: model and cloud suppliers, regulators, courts, affected parties, adversaries.
frames.viability_question: Can the enterprise let agents act autonomously while keeping control, independent assurance, adaptation and a working alarm channel?

roles.rationale: Performs the primary operational activity; stands for any number of S1 units, each recursively viable
Operational substrate where activity lands; source of algedonic signals. Debatable: could be treated as environment
Arbitrates tool and protocol access across agents
Arbitrates identity and delegation across agents
Operational control, scope enforcement, accountability
Accountability record for S3
In its oversight capacity only: human override and supervision
Independent probing outside the S3 command line
Scans models, vendors, regulation and incidents
Legal principal; holds identity and ultimate policy

frames.label: Global AI governance as a network of regimes (recursion level +1)
frames.description: Treated as one meta-system of interacting regimes (EU, US, China, UK, APAC). Per-regime frames are a possible extension.
frames.system_boundary: Inside: deployers, providers and platforms, and the institutions that legislate, regulate, adjudicate, standardise, evaluate and audit them. Outside (resource suppliers or environment): capital, silicon, energy, compute, data, adversaries, affected populations, civil society.
frames.viability_question: Can the network of regimes sense harm, adapt policy and enforce it fast enough relative to the pace of AI deployment?

views.title: Value chain, power and physical limits
views.question: Where do power and margin concentrate across the stack, and which links are physically or politically constrained?

views.title: Enterprise AI operation viability
views.question: Are all five VSM systems present and connected, and is the algedonic channel intact, for one enterprise's AI operations?

views.title: Societal governance viability
views.question: Which governance functions and channels exist at the regime level, and where are the gaps or single points of failure?

views.title: Harm, liability and recourse
views.question: When an agent causes harm, who bears liability, and where does recourse break?

views.title: Protocol planes and lock-in
views.question: Which protocol planes bind the agent stack, and where is lock-in concentrated?

views.title: Feedback structure
views.question: Which loops drive concentration, and which provide correction?

views.title: Continuing assurance
views.question: When a certified deployment changes or produces adverse evidence, can reassessment be triggered by credible and independent evidence, and who can rely on the result?

views.title: Adversarial surface
views.question: Where can adversaries act, and which controls and audit channels stand in the way?
